summary:
I developed SPHEREx Sky Viewer, a web application for searching, downloading and visualising real SPHEREx infrared observations from NASA/IPAC’s IRSA archive.
Users enter a sky position, radius and collection, and the backend finds matching observations, groups detector files into telescope pointings, and downloads the original FITS files on demand.
Each file is validated with Astropy and rendered as an interactive preview with zoom, pixel-value and sky-coordinate probing, an extension and header inspector, and a chronological flipbook for comparing observations over time.
This addresses the difficulty of working with large, specialised FITS data by replacing code-based steps with a simple browser workflow, while using real archive data only and keeping original files unmodified.
details:
SPHEREx Sky Viewer is a web app for searching, downloading and visualising real SPHEREx infrared observations from NASA/IPAC’s IRSA archive.
Users enter a sky position, radius and collection, and the FastAPI backend queries IRSA and groups detector files into telescope pointings.
Selected FITS files are downloaded, validated with Astropy and rendered as preview images that users can zoom, probe pixel by pixel, and inspect extension by extension.
A chronological flipbook plays observations in time order so changes across a region of sky are easy to compare.
It is built with Next.js, React and Tailwind on the frontend and FastAPI, Astropy and SQLite on the backend, and uses real archive data only.
